cases_inside_tolerance: one sector per fuel, by construction
best_case_tuned_single_constant.description: one constant per fuel, TUNED by exhaustive sweep to pass as many graded cases as possible.
best_case_tuned_single_constant.min_gap_multiple_scored_over: not applicable - a tuned sweep, not a route
best_case_tuned_single_constant.non_discriminating_note: See note: reachable only with the withheld table, and bounded at one case per fuel.
best_case_tuned_single_constant.note: Not a competing method - an adversarial lower bound on luck, measured rather than assumed. With one constant per fuel and one graded case per consuming sector, a tuned constant can always match at most one sector per fuel, and the values it must land on (coal 20.2800, petroleum_products 4.5675) ARE sector heat contents, so the route is only reachable with the withheld table already in hand. The realistic untuned constants - 5.8, 5.77, 20, 24, 19 - are measured separately and miss every graded case.

coke_plants_take_other_industrial_row.description: coke plants graded on the OTHER-industrial coal row rather than the coke plants row - the mis-selection available inside the right table.
coke_plants_take_other_industrial_row.non_discriminating_note: MEASURED: this route lands inside tolerance on 4 of 5 graded case(s) (group-petroleum_products-residential, group-petroleum_products-commercial, group-petroleum_products-industrial, group-coal-commercial), of which 0 are cases the route actually alters. Recorded rather than hidden. It is not a free pass for an unaided run: every case it clears still needs the consuming-sector factor table, which is the withheld lever - this route only mis-selects WITHIN that table, so it is reachable only with the table in hand.
coke_plants_take_other_industrial_row.note: A real competing method: 'industrial coal' reads as one sector, and the publisher splits it into coke plants and other industrial.

electric_power_sector_row.description: use the electric power sector's row for every consuming sector - the most widely quoted row of the table, because power-sector fuel accounting is where these factors are usually met.
electric_power_sector_row.note: A real competing method: the power-sector row is the one an analyst has most often seen quoted, so it is the wrong row that gets reused.

generic_crude_equivalent.description: one textbook per-fuel constant for everything: 5.8 million Btu per barrel of crude oil equivalent and 20 million Btu per short ton of coal. This is the route with no published factor table at all, and it is the figure question.json carries as its labelled orientation block.
generic_crude_equivalent.note: A real competing method: the crude-oil-equivalent and round-number coal constants are what an analyst without the sector table actually reaches for, and they are the shipped orientation figure.

one_row_reused_for_every_sector.description: the table is found, but ONE row of it is applied to every consuming sector of that fuel - the residential petroleum row for all petroleum and the coke plants row for all coal.
one_row_reused_for_every_sector.non_discriminating_note: MEASURED: this route lands inside tolerance on 2 of 5 graded case(s) (group-petroleum_products-residential, group-coal-industrial_coke_plants), of which 0 are cases the route actually alters. Recorded rather than hidden. It is not a free pass for an unaided run: every case it clears still needs the consuming-sector factor table, which is the withheld lever - this route only mis-selects WITHIN that table, so it is reachable only with the table in hand.
one_row_reused_for_every_sector.note: A real competing method, and the closest neighbour of the right answer: it uses the publisher's own year-specific values and gets the sector dimension - the whole lever - wrong.

product_level_shortcut.description: distillate fuel oil's published heat content for every petroleum barrel and 24 million Btu per short ton for every ton of coal.
product_level_shortcut.note: A real competing method: substituting the dominant PRODUCT's factor for the consuming sector's product-mix factor.

published_all_sector_average.description: use EIA's published ALL-SECTOR heat content for each fuel and year - the aggregate row of the same table - instead of the consuming sector's own row.
published_all_sector_average.note: The nearest real competitor: an analyst who finds the publisher's Appendix A but takes the aggregate row rather than the row for the consuming sector. Not a strawman - it is the same table, one line off.

residential_commercial_swapped.description: the residential and commercial petroleum rows exchanged.
residential_commercial_swapped.non_discriminating_note: MEASURED: this route lands inside tolerance on 3 of 5 graded case(s) (group-petroleum_products-industrial, group-coal-commercial, group-coal-industrial_coke_plants), of which 0 are cases the route actually alters. Recorded rather than hidden. It is not a free pass for an unaided run: every case it clears still needs the consuming-sector factor table, which is the withheld lever - this route only mis-selects WITHIN that table, so it is reachable only with the table in hand.

single_vintage_final_year.description: right consuming sector, but the final year's factor applied to every year of the window instead of each year's own.
single_vintage_final_year.non_discriminating_note: MEASURED: this route lands inside tolerance on 2 of 5 graded case(s) (group-petroleum_products-residential, group-coal-industrial_coke_plants), of which 2 are cases the route actually alters. Recorded rather than hidden. It is not a free pass for an unaided run: every case it clears still needs the consuming-sector factor table, which is the withheld lever - this route only mis-selects WITHIN that table, so it is reachable only with the table in hand.
single_vintage_final_year.note: A real competing method: taking the latest published column of the table and carrying it back over the whole window.

sum_quantities_then_convert_once.description: total each book's physical quantities first and convert once, with the arithmetic mean of that book's own published series, instead of converting row by row.
sum_quantities_then_convert_once.non_discriminating_note: MEASURED: lands inside tolerance on 4 of 5 graded case(s) (group-petroleum_products-residential, group-petroleum_products-commercial, group-petroleum_products-industrial, group-coal-industrial_coke_plants). Recorded rather than hidden. The book it clears is the one whose quantity profile happens to sit near the unweighted mean of its own series; the other books miss. It is not a free pass for an unaided run either - taking the arithmetic mean of a book's series requires the withheld table in hand.
sum_quantities_then_convert_once.note: A real competing method: it is the shortcut a run takes when it has the table but treats the year index as a detail. It is an AGGREGATION-order error, not a factor error, so it is measured separately from the factor routes.

method: each ledger row converted with the heat content published for that fuel, that CONSUMING SECTOR and that year, then summed by group, by year and over the whole portfolio
published_precision_ambiguity_method: MEASURED, not asserted: every graded figure re-derived through the independent formulation (sector factors implied by EIA's separately published sector energy series, and solved from the published all-sector heat content identity where the energy series is on the biofuel-excluded basis), and the worst relative disagreement against the golden taken over all 5 cases.
tolerance_rationale: One relative tolerance, 1.0 percent of the reference, applied to every graded figure as an absolute band stored per case. LOWER BOUND (defensible-reading spread): zero. The ledger carries exact quantities and the publisher's factors are exact decimals, so two faithful readings of the same published inputs cannot differ at all; the measured spread of the INDEPENDENT re-derivation - factors implied by separately published EIA energy series rather than read off Appendix A - is 0.0448 percent, well inside the band. UPPER BOUND (nearest wrong route): the nearest real competitor, taking the publisher's ALL-SECTOR row instead of the consuming sector's own, sits 2.79 tolerances away on its closest graded case, and every graded case clears the 2x floor. The band is therefore wide enough that no faithful reading fails and narrow enough that no competing method passes.
